answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may post a bid, with the lock held until the transaction is settled and a challenge window closes. Splitting funds across a thousand identities then does not create a thousand free votes: each identity ties up capital, and dishonest bids can forfeit the bond. The cost scales with attempted influence, while the attacker also loses liquidity and risks slashing. Even on a dune, at nadir activity or across a delta of markets, the same stake rule applies.
